facts.text: The superb parrot is also known as Barraband's parrot or the green leek parrot.
facts.quote: The superb parrot (Polytelis swainsonii), also known as Barraband's parrot, Barraband's parakeet, or green leek parrot, is a parrot native to south-eastern Australia.

facts.text: It is mostly bright green with darker flight feathers and a long pointed tail.
facts.quote: The superb parrot is mostly bright green with darker flight feathers and is about 40 cm (16 in) long with a long pointed tail.

facts.text: Adult males have a yellow forehead and throat with a red band across the border of the throat.
facts.quote: Adult males have continuous yellow foreheads and throats, with a red horizontal band across the border of the throat.

facts.text: Adult females have a pale blue-green face, greyish-green throat, and orange thighs.
facts.quote: The adult female has a pale blue-green face, greyish-green throat, a variable tinged russet-pink fore-throat, and orange thighs.

facts.text: During breeding season, small flocks of males often forage for food alone.
facts.quote: During breeding season, small flocks of males often forage for food alone.

facts.text: It mainly eats eucalypt flowers, fruits, nectar and pollen, including seeds of the yellow box.
facts.quote: The diet consists mainly of eucalypt flowers, fruits, nectar and pollen. It consumes seeds and green heads of the yellow box (Eucalyptus melliodora).

facts.text: The superb parrot lives in the dry woodlands of New South Wales and Victoria, with at least 10,000 individuals in the wild.
facts.quote: the superb parrot is restricted to the dry (sclerophyll) woodlands of New South Wales and Victoria. There is estimated to be at least 10,000 individuals in the wild.

facts.text: It was listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List until being downlisted to Least Concern in 2012.
facts.quote: the superb parrot was evaluated as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, until it was downlisted to Least Concern in 2012.

facts.text: Logging in Barmah State Forest in 2005 destroyed 60 percent of its nesting colonies.
facts.quote: During February–June 2005, timber logging in the Barmah State Forest destroyed 60 percent of the nesting colonies of the superb parrot
